samples.summary: Toggle-off now emits a Yorkie `removeStyleByPath` op on the hottest editing path (B/I/U/S); if Yorkie history cannot reverse TreeStyleRemove, Cmd+Z after a toggle-off silently stops restoring the flag
samples.evidence: With the demotion in `Doc.styleOffAsClear`, every B/I/U/S off-toggle now reaches `YorkieDocStore.applyStyleInTree` with the key set to `undefined`, so `removedInlineStyleAttrs` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:144-163) returns the attr and `tree.removeStyleByPath(...)` runs at yorkie-doc-store.ts:1881 — previously only `styleByPath` ran for a toggle-off (the `false` was serialized), and `removeStyleByPath` was reached only by the rare removeLink / clear-formatting paths. Docs undo is Yorkie-history based (`this.doc.history.undo()` at yorkie-doc-store.ts:2611), so the reversibility of the removeStyle op is now load-bearing for the most common formatting action in the product. I could not verify the SDK's reverse-op support from this checkout (the Yorkie SDK is not installed in node_modules here); confirming needs a collab/integration run that toggles bold off and then undoes it against a real Yorkie doc. Fix, if real, belongs in the Yorkie store (emit a compensating style write) rather than in the new Doc code.

samples.summary: The new demotion lives in `Doc`, so the store-level `applyStyle`/`applyStyles` entry points still write a raw `false`; the interface doc actively steers callers to the bypassing one
samples.evidence: `DocStore.applyStyles()` (packages/docs/src/store/store.ts:84-90) is documented as 'Prefer this over looping applyStyle() whenever …', and two live callers already skip `Doc` entirely: packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1095 and packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:907. Both write only `{ fontSize }` today, so nothing is broken right now, but any boolean write routed through `docStore.applyStyle`/`applyStyles` (or through a new store client) re-introduces exactly the dead `false` flag this change removes, because `styleOffAsClear` is only applied in packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:377 and :431. Placing the demotion in `block-helpers.applyInlineStyle` (which every store already funnels through) would close the bypass.

samples.summary: Agent charters and a harness oracle still document the old contract ('docs leaves an explicit `false` behind') as ground truth, which will now generate false findings
samples.evidence: scripts/agent/charters-ui/sheet-author.md:84-85 tells exploring agents 'This is also where the sheet surface DIFFERS from docs, where the same round trip leaves an explicit `false` behind (#749, #793). Do not carry that expectation across.' — after this change the docs round trip clears the key, so the brief is wrong in the direction most likely to cost a violated prediction. Same stale statement at scripts/agent/charters-ui/doc-writer.md:117 ('#749 stores `italic:false`'), the mirrored copies under .trusted/scripts/agent/charters-ui/, and the comment at packages/frontend/scripts/verify-hunt-oracles.mjs:592. None of these are covered by an enforced lane (they are prose/comments), so nothing else will catch the drift.

samples.summary: `styleOffAsClear` adds a `findBlock()` lookup inside the per-block style-write loop, turning a toggle-off over a large selection into a quadratic scan
samples.evidence: `this.findBlock(blockId)` (document.ts:405) scans `this._document.blocks` linearly (document.ts:177) and, for a cell-internal block whose entry is missing from the layout-time `_blockParentMap`, falls back to a full recursive walk of every table in body/header/footer (`findBlockInCells`, document.ts:214-220). This now runs once per visited block slice for every `visitRangeSlices`/`visitCellRectangleSlices` write that contains a `false` — i.e. every Cmd+B-off over a multi-block selection or a large cell rectangle, which previously did no block lookup at all. Caching the resolved defaults per blockId (or hoisting the lookup out of the visitor) would avoid the O(n²) shape.

samples.summary: Clearing the key lets the local cache re-merge runs the Yorkie Tree keeps split, and the tree→block parser does not normalize, so a reload or a remote peer sees a different run structure than the writer
samples.evidence: `applyInlineStyleHelper` (now with `mergeInlineStyle` deleting the key) makes `normalizeInlines` re-merge the neighbours, so `YorkieDocStore.applyStyle`'s cache update (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1707/1720) stores one run while the Tree still holds three identically-styled inline nodes (the todo at docs/tasks/active/20260819-docs-inline-style-off-clears-key-todo.md:62 lists tree merging as a non-goal). `treeNodeToBlock` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:418-426) does not merge equal-styled inlines, so a peer or a page reload parses three runs where the local writer's cache has one. Anything reading run structure per-run rather than per-character — e.g. the hunt reader `doc.runs` (packages/frontend/src/app/harness/hunt/bridge.ts:143) — will report differently before and after a refresh.

verdict.reason: Every structural element of the claim checks out. `styleOffAsClear` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:399-418) demotes `false`→`undefined` for BOOLEAN_INLINE_STYLE_KEYS (document.ts:39-45) on both write paths (document.ts:377, 431). That `undefined` is picked up by `removedInlineStyleAttrs` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:144-163, which matches on `key in style && style[key] === undefined`) and drives `tree.removeStyleByPath(...)` at yorkie-doc-store.ts:1881, reachable from both `applyStyle` (:1716) and `applyStyleBatch` (:1760) with no intervening guard. The claim that this is new for toggle-off is also correct: `serializeInlineStyle` serializes a literal `false` via `setIfDefined` (:108-113), so previously only `styleByPath` ran. Undo is genuinely Yorkie-history based (`this.doc.history.undo()` at :2611), so op reversibility is load-bearing. I could not confirm or disconfirm whether the SDK reverses a TreeStyleRemove: `@yorkie-js/sdk` 0.7.16 (packages/frontend/package.json:93) is not installed (no node_modules), and existing undo coverage only exercises the additive `styleByPath` case (tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:197-207) — no test covers undo after a removeStyleByPath. The same test file documents other Yorkie Tree undo gaps via `TODO(yorkie-undo)` skips (:221-223, :275-279), so the risk class is real in this codebase. No refutation ground applies: code present as described, reachable, and a changed write contract breaking a downstream consumer (history/undo) is in the blast-radius lane. Uncertainty is only about the SDK's behaviour, which keeps the finding.
